title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
abstract: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.

bite.hook: Researchers derive an explicit quantum logarithmic Sobolev constant directly from conditional hyperboundedness.
tldr: Studied relative entropy contraction rates for finite-dimensional quantum channels and KMS-symmetric Markov semigroups.
Combined conditional hyperboundedness with GNS contraction to derive explicit modified logarithmic Sobolev constants.
Established that completely bounded hyperboundedness extends entropy contraction bounds to auxiliary quantum systems.
bite.whyItMatters: Logarithmic Sobolev inequalities govern how quickly noisy open quantum systems lose information and reach thermal equilibrium, which is critical for understanding quantum memory fidelity.
bite.eli5: When a warm room cools down, heat flows out at a predictable speed. This paper gives an exact mathematical formula for how fast quantum information leaks into its surroundings, guaranteeing the decay rate holds true even with extra spectator particles.
